title: Invited: Human-Inspired Distributed Wearable AI
problem: Wearable AI devices face significant technical bottlenecks in power efficiency, processing capability, and form-factor constraints that prevent deployment of continuous AI inference. Current systems struggle to enable distributed AI processing across heterogeneous wearable hardware.
motivation: The convergence of human-AI interaction with wearable technology creates urgent research needs to enable practical AI capabilities within strict power and size budgets of wearable devices for health monitoring and productivity applications.
method: Vision paper addressing distributed, human-inspired approaches to wearable AI. Discusses architectural paradigms for resource-constrained edge processing and integration across multiple wearable devices with heterogeneous capabilities.
key_novelty: Human-inspired distributed AI processing architecture specifically optimized for wearable form factors and energy constraints.
contributions: Identifies and characterizes technical bottlenecks in wearable AI systems
Presents vision for distributed wearable AI architecture
Discusses human-inspired computing principles for edge devices
limitations: Abstract does not discuss specific methods, benchmarks, or evaluation results
